1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Hollin Vale Bank is a fictional regional lender with 19 branches across the Maddern Valley. Branch loan officers take in small-business (SME) loan applications and collect the documents. All SME credit decisions are made centrally by the Credit Hub in Kestwick. In the second quarter the bank moved to a new loan-origination system (Corvane Origination), renewed its contract with its only valuation panel firm, refreshed its credit policy, and replaced five departing SME loan officers.
9	Your request: The COO wants to know why SME loan approvals have taken longer since the spring and what the bank should do. Her month-end decision paper covers the Corvane contract and the performance of the new hires.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Email from Imogen Raye, COO, to the executive team, 1 September (leadership-account): Subject: SME approvals. Since we switched to Corvane in April, our small-business approval times have nearly doubled: 13 days in August against 7 in March. On top of that we lost five experienced loan officers in Q2, and the replacements are still learning. By month-end I want two things. First, a decision paper on whether we withhold Corvane's final milestone payment and go back to the legacy workflow. Second, a plan from HR, with targets, to get the new hires up to speed. Customers are noticing, and withdrawals are up too.
12	- Monthly lending dashboard, SME loans, March–August (system-record): Median business days from application to decision, Mar–Aug: 7.2, 8.0, 9.6, 11.8, 13.1, 13.4. Applications received: 212, 205, 219, 224, 231, 228. Withdrawn before decision: 6.1%, 6.4%, 7.0%, 8.2%, 8.9%, 8.5%. Consumer loans (same branches, on Corvane since April), median days: 3.9, 4.6, 4.2, 4.0, 4.1, 4.0. The SME median rose at 18 of 19 branches. Footnote: since the Corvane cutover (14 April), SME applications with no customer document upload for 30 calendar days are auto-closed and counted as withdrawn. The legacy system left such files open indefinitely.
13	- HR summary for the COO, 22 August (document): SME loan officers: 34 at 1 April. Leavers April–June: 5 (3 retirements, 2 resignations to a competitor), average tenure 14 years. Replacements started between 6 May and 17 June at Ashby North, Brenmoor, Calder Quay, Hythe Lane and Overstrand. Two are internal transfers from consumer lending. All five completed the three-week Corvane and credit-procedures induction. Headcount was back to 34 by 17 June. Branch lending authorities are unchanged: the Credit Hub still makes all SME credit decisions centrally.
14	- Interview notes, Dev Okafor, Brenmoor branch manager, 26 August (manager-account): 'Corvane was painful in April. We were scanning everything twice and logins kept dropping. That's mostly settled now. The real problem starts once a file goes to the Hub. The status just says "With Credit Hub", it sits there a week or more, and then it comes back approved. Nobody tells us what they're doing. My new officer is fine on paperwork; on the system she's quicker than the man she replaced.' Asked whether all SME files are affected equally: 'Feels like it, but I haven't checked.'
15	- Operations change calendar, Q2 (extract) (change-record): 1 Apr – Valuation panel contract renewed with Pellow & Strand Valuers (sole panel firm). New fee schedule; service levels unchanged. 14 Apr – Corvane Origination goes live at all branches for consumer and SME lending. 1 May – Credit Policy v14 takes effect (annual refresh). Credit Policy Unit note: 'Largely editorial; no change to approval authorities or pricing.' 6 May–17 Jun – five replacement SME loan officers start (see HR summary). 3 Jun – one Credit Hub SME underwriter goes on parental leave; a contractor covers until November.
16	
17	BRIEF:
18	The delay is mostly one thing: since 1 May the credit policy requires a full inspection appraisal for property collateral between $150k and $500k, where a quick desktop valuation used to be allowed. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the valuation firm, against about 1.2 for desktop ones. The valuation stage for property-secured loans rose from 1.6 to 8.4 days, and every order in that band carries the policy code. Unsecured loans are back near their March times (5.9 vs 5.6 days). The valuation firm's turnaround per type of valuation has not changed. The new system caused a brief April bump that has since cleared. New hires' branches show the same document-collection times as other branches. Hub staffing and volume do not explain the rise. Policy's impact on processing times was never assessed. Withdrawals rose, but part of that comes from the new 30-day auto-close rule, so I can't yet tell how much is due to slower approvals. Recommended: don't withhold Corvane's payment, don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Instead, take the measured delay to the credit risk committee, alongside the audit finding that justified the rule, and ask them to decide whether to keep or adjust it. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard. Hold off on fee rebates until the withdrawal causes are split out.
19
